policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV opens 'Take heed that ye do not your righteousness' with no connective; a transitional δὲ is left untranslated either way, so the English does not distinguish presence from omission.
ASV reads 'your righteousness', rendering δικαιοσύνην; ἐλεημοσύνην would have given 'alms', which ASV uses only later in v. 2-4.
ASV 'and thy Father who seeth in secret shall recompense thee' has no intensive 'himself'; the added αὑτὸς is unrepresented.
ASV ends 'shall recompense thee' with no 'openly'; the added ἐν τῷ φανερῷ is unrepresented.

ASV 'And when ye pray, ye shall not be as the hypocrites' is plural throughout, excluding RP's singular προσεύχῃ ... ἔσῃ (r02); the remaining readings differ only in punctuation spacing, which the English cannot distinguish.
ASV 'that they may be seen of men' renders ὅπως alone; the particle ἄν adds nothing renderable to a purpose clause, so the English does not distinguish the readings.
ASV 'Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward' presents direct discourse; a recitative ὅτι before quoted speech goes untranslated, so the English does not distinguish the readings.
ASV ends 'shall recompense thee' with no 'openly'; the added ἐν τῷ φανερῷ is unrepresented.

ASV text reads 'your Father' without θεὸς, and the mapped textual note 'Some ancient authorities read God your Father' explicitly assigns the longer reading to other authorities rather than to the text rendered.
ASV 'as in heaven, so on earth' renders ἐπὶ γῆς identically with or without the article τῆς, which English does not mark.
ASV 'as we also have forgiven our debtors' is a completed past, rendering the aorist ἀφήκαμεν; the present ἀφίεμεν would give 'as we forgive'.
ASV ends the prayer at 'deliver us from the evil one' with no doxology; the note here is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, evil') and concerns πονηροῦ only.
ASV 'But if ye forgive not men their trespasses' renders τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν; the short reading would end at 'forgive not men'.
ASV 'as the hypocrites' renders ὡς and ὥσπερ alike; the English does not distinguish the comparative particles.
ASV 'Verily I say unto you, They have received their reward' presents direct discourse; a recitative ὅτι goes untranslated, so the English does not distinguish the readings.
ASV 'thy Father who is in secret' renders κρυφαίῳ and κρυπτῷ identically; the synonyms are not distinguished in English.
ASV 'who seeth in secret' renders κρυφαίῳ and κρυπτῷ identically; the synonyms are not distinguished in English.
ASV 'where thy treasure is' is singular, rendering σου; ὑμῶν would give 'your treasure' in ASV's consistent thou/ye distinction.
ASV 'there will thy heart be also' is singular, rendering σου; ὑμῶν would give 'your heart' in ASV's consistent thou/ye distinction.
ASV 'if therefore thine eye be single' fixes English clause order regardless of where the Greek verb ῃ stands; the variant is word order only and the English does not distinguish it.
ASV 'what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink' renders the disjunctive ἢ τί πίητε; the short reading omits the clause and RP's καὶ τί πίητε would give 'and what ye shall drink'.

ASV 'how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin' is plural, excluding RP's singular αὐξάνει ... κοπιᾷ ... νήθει (r03); the remaining readings differ only in punctuation and the κοπιῶσιν/κοπιοῦσιν spelling, which 'they toil not' does not distinguish.

ASV 'do the Gentiles seek' takes a plural English verb with the plural subject 'the Gentiles', but Greek τὰ ἔθνη is neuter plural and regularly takes a singular verb; both ἐπιζητοῦσιν and ἐπιζητεῖ yield this rendering.
ASV 'seek ye first his kingdom' has the possessive αὐτοῦ and no 'of God'; the added τοῦ θεοῦ is unrepresented.

ASV 'the morrow will be anxious for itself' has a bare reflexive, excluding RP's τὰ ἑαυτῆς ('for its own things', r02); the remaining readings differ only in breathing and contraction of the same pronoun.
